churches.assessment: Anglican Church of the Ascension in Indianapolis is an ACNA parish in the Anglican Diocese of the Living Word, led by Rector Rev. Timothy Felch. The congregation meets at Fortune Academy on the east side of Indianapolis with a 9:30 AM Sunday service. The parish vision is 'to build a liturgical community in the Anglican Tradition, welcoming of the stranger, where Christ is proclaimed and made manifest in our lives.' ACNA operates under the 39 Articles of Religion and the Book of Common Prayer confessional framework with a formal male-only ordination policy — which aligns cleanly with MOOP's biblical-design rubric. Green-rated orthodox Anglican option for the Indianapolis metro.

churches.assessment: First Baptist Hammond is one of the most controversial churches in American Christianity. Founded 1887, it became a megachurch under Jack Hyles. The church has been plagued by scandals: Jack Schaap (Hyles' successor and son-in-law) was convicted of transporting a minor across state lines for sexual activity (2012). Multiple staff/associated pastors have faced similar charges. The institutional culture has been widely criticized for prioritizing numbers, easy-believism, and personality-driven leadership over genuine accountability. Current pastor John Wilkerson has attempted to restore credibility, but the institutional DNA remains a major concern. NOT recommended without extensive personal investigation.

churches.assessment: First Baptist Church of Hammond is the historic Hyles-Anderson legacy IFB congregation in Hammond, IN. The church is tied to Hyles-Anderson College and was led by Jack Hyles from 1959 until his death in 2001, then by his son-in-law Jack Schaap from 2001 until Schaap's 2012 conviction for sexual misconduct with a 16-year-old church member (he served prison time and was released 2021). Multiple women have publicly described abuse and cover-up patterns spanning decades of the Hyles era. Current senior pastor John Wilkerson (since 2013) inherited the institution at its lowest reputational point and has publicly acknowledged the failures while leading reform. The congregation is included for completeness as one of the most consequential IFB institutions in the country, but is rated YELLOW with significant caution: the documented abuse history, Hyles-era pastor-as-king theology, and KJV-Only doctrinal emphasis all warrant discernment. Adam should not visit casually; survivors of Hyles/Schaap-era abuse remain a live pastoral concern within IFB circles.
churches.gender_detail: Patriarchal — male pastors/deacons; Hyles-era 'manhood' teaching legacy (verify reform)

churches.assessment: Saint Joseph Parish in South Bend is the Roman Catholic parish where Justice Amy Coney Barrett is a longtime member — she served as Council Chair for two one-year terms between 2013 and June 2015, providing counsel to the pastor and assisting in parish duties. Founded 1853, the parish is in the Diocese of Fort Wayne–South Bend and is pastored by the Congregation of Holy Cross (C.S.C.) — the same religious order that runs the University of Notre Dame, where Justice Barrett taught law for years. Current pastor Fr. Matt Fase, C.S.C. The parish operates a robust parochial Pre-K through 8th grade school, a Totus Tuus summer faith program (grades 1-12), and the Catechesis of the Good Shepherd children's formation program. Theologically the parish holds the historic Catholic positions: Nicene Christology, male-only priesthood, sacramental soteriology, traditional sexual ethics. MOOP's rubric is built around Protestant confessional categories, so Catholic parishes register as yellow with a denominational note. Within the Catholic tradition, Saint Joseph South Bend is a serious, orthodox parish tied to the Holy Cross + Notre Dame tradition.

churches.assessment: Winona Lake Grace Church sits in the Indiana college-and-seminary town that serves as the geographic hub of the Charis Fellowship — Grace College, Grace Theological Seminary, and the national Charis office are all in Winona Lake. Lead Pastor Kip Cone is Grace College and Grace Seminary trained, served almost a decade as a missionary in Berlin, Germany with Encompass World Partners (formerly Grace Brethren International Missions), and has been on the church's pastoral staff since 2006. The Charis Fellowship is dispensational evangelical-Anabaptist, complementarian, biblically-inerrantist. For a northern-Indiana man wanting a Bible-rooted, mission-minded Grace Brethren church in the heart of the denomination's institutional life, Winona Lake Grace deserves a careful look.
